name_note: GTDB's g__Coprococcus also contains genomes labelled Clostridium and a few labelled Akkermansia by NCBI, so it is somewhat broader than the classical genus.

sentences.text: Coprococcus is related to butyrate-producing bacteria found in human faeces, which are highly oxygen-sensitive anaerobes belonging to Clostridial clusters IV and XIVa.
Butyrate arising from microbial fermentation is described as important for the energy metabolism and normal development of colonic epithelial cells.
A study reported that Coprococcus bacteria were consistently associated with higher quality of life indicators and were depleted in depression, even after correcting for antidepressant effects.
A meta-analysis reported depleted Coprococcus across several psychiatric disorders, and other studies reported it less abundant in faeces of Parkinson's disease patients and in autistic children.
